functions.name: VehicleWheelContactHeightCheck
functions.summary: Computes the wheel contact patch position and its terrain penetration for a vehicle wheel. Takes a wheel-geometry array a2 (origin a2[0..2], length-scale, direction a2[8..10]) and a contact-type selector a4; writes the contact position, a half-extent probe frame and final suspension-compression/lateral-tilt values into the output a3. Computes a3[0..2] = a2[0..2] + scale * a2[8..10] where scale is a2[7] (a4==1) or a2[6] / a2[71]+a2[6] (other paths), then scales a direction vector by half of a scalar read from this (this[1] on the a4==1 path, *this elsewhere) to build the a3[3..5] half-extent. Queries SpatialGridQuery at the contact center and at plus/minus the half-extent, resolves side-height disagreement beyond a 0.35 threshold by mirroring the farther sample, then writes a3[1] = max(center, average of sides) + 0.06 and a3[4] = half the side-height difference.

operations.description: Dispatch on a4 (contact-type selector): a4 == 1 takes the steering-aligned path using a2[7] as the scale; a4 == 0 selects the extended-spring length a2[71] + a2[6]; any other non-zero a4 uses a2[6] alone.
Contact-point computation: a3[0..2] = a2[0..2] + scale * a2[8..10], where scale is a2[7] on the a4 == 1 path and v5 (a2[6] or a2[71] + a2[6]) on the other paths.
Write the computed contact position into the output a3 (a3[0], a3[1], a3[2]).
Half-extent frame: read the scalar v8 from this — this[1] on the a4 == 1 path, *this otherwise — and set a3[3..5] = (v8 * 0.5) * a2[8..10].
SpatialGridQuery(&v46): terrain-height query at the contact position a3 (v46 = {a3[0], a3[1], a3[2]}); on success the returned height is captured in v53 (v29 = v53).
SpatialGridQuery at the low-side probe (a3[0]-a3[3], a3[1], a3[2]-a3[5]); the returned height v30 falls back to the center height v29 when the query fails.
SpatialGridQuery at the high-side probe (a3[0]+a3[3], a3[1], a3[2]+a3[5]); the returned height v25 falls back to v29 when the query fails.

Side-sample consistency: when v25 differs from (2 * v29 - v30) by more than 0.35, keep the side sample closer to the center and mirror the farther one (v30 = 2 * v29 - v25 or v25 = 2 * v29 - v30) so both sides agree with the center height.
Average the two side heights v28 = (v30 + v25) * 0.5, then clamp v28 to be at least the center height (v28 = v29 when v29 > v28).
Update the contact state in a3: a3[1] = v28 + 0.06 (compressed suspension height) and a3[4] = (v25 - v30) * 0.5 (lateral tilt from the side-height difference).

Read-only scalar constants loaded from the globals 0x0059E450, 0x0059E454, 0x0059E458 and 0x007C9360 and consumed by the half-extent, threshold and lift arithmetic (the raw source renders the float constants as literals such as 0.5, 0.34999999 and 0.059999999).

functions.name: VehicleWheelPhaseProcessor
functions.summary: Time-sliced three-phase state machine that processes vehicle wheel data across multiple frames. Computes a target grip-derived value v9 = 1.0 - (flt_8AFEE8 + flt_8AFEEC) * 0.5 and enters the processing path when the stored float at this+0x170 differs from v9 beyond tolerance or the index at this+0x174 is not the idle sentinel -1. Each call processes a batch of at most 20 wheels: phase selector this+0x16C == 0 runs friction callback sub_4FB260(v9), == 1 runs suspension callback sub_4FAF60, == 2 runs VehicleProximity; the phase index advances in this+0x174 and a phase transition occurs only when a batch reaches the wheel count at this+0x130. Enter processing if |float(this+0x170) - v9| > 0.05 or this+0x174 != -1; -1 is the idle sentinel for the phase index.
Re-initialize the machine when idle: set this+0x174 = 0, store v9 into float(this+0x170), and set phase selector this+0x16C = 0.
Compute batch end bound v3 = min(this+0x174 + 20, wheel count at this+0x130).
Dispatch on phase selector this+0x16C: 0 = friction, 1 = suspension, 2 = proximity.
Phase 0: for each wheel index in [this+0x174, v3) call sub_4FB260(v9) and advance this+0x174.
Phase 0 completion: when v3 reaches this+0x130, set this+0x16C = 1 and reset this+0x174 = 0.
Phase 1: for each wheel index in [this+0x174, v3) call sub_4FAF60 on wheel array base this+0x134 + 316 * index and advance this+0x174.
Phase 1 completion: when v3 reaches this+0x130, set this+0x174 = 0 and this+0x16C = 2.
Phase 2: for each wheel index in [this+0x174, v3) call VehicleProximity on wheel array base this+0x134 + 316 * index and advance this+0x174.
Phase 2 completion: when v3 reaches this+0x130, set this+0x16C = 0 and this+0x174 = -1, returning the machine to idle.
